issues.description: Command names in feature tests don't match registered commands (underscore vs hyphen mismatch)
issues.detail: The Python methods are `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload`, which qutebrowser typically registers with underscores converted to hyphens, giving `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload`. However, other existing commands here follow a singular pattern (`quickmark_save` -> `:quickmark-save`, `bookmark_add`). Using plural `quickmarks-reload` breaks naming consistency with the rest of the command surface and may surprise users.

issues.description: reload() called before save-manager init may race with pending in-memory changes
issues.detail: In `__init__`, `reload()` now runs before `_init_savemanager`. If a user invokes `:bookmarks-reload` after making unsaved in-memory changes (e.g., adding a bookmark not yet flushed), `reload()` clears `marks` and re-reads from disk, silently discarding pending changes. Consider documenting this or saving first.

issues.description: Missing doc/changelog entry for new user-facing commands
issues.detail: Two new commands (`quickmarks-reload`, `bookmarks-reload`) are added but there's no update to doc/changelog.asciidoc or the commands documentation. qutebrowser's contribution conventions typically require these for new commands so users can discover the feature.

issues.description: Feature test scenarios lack descriptive names
issues.detail: The new Gherkin scenarios use bare `Scenario:` with no title, unlike every other scenario in the file (e.g., "Saving a quickmark (:quickmark-add)"). This hurts readability of test output and breaks the file's convention.

issues.description: Unit test doesn't verify quickmark-specific reload behavior
issues.detail: `test_reload` only exercises `BookmarkManager`. `QuickmarkManager` overrides `_parse_line` and `clear` with different semantics (emits `removed` per mark). A reload test for QuickmarkManager would catch regressions in signal emission ordering for quickmarks specifically.

`QuickmarkManager.clear()` likely emits `removed` for each entry, but `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` directly (the dict method), bypassing the override. Any UI listening for `removed` signals (e.g., completion models) may not refresh stale entries until `changed` propagates.

review.summary: The PR adds useful `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload` commands by refactoring init into a reusable `reload()` method. The main concern is the command naming inconsistency (plural vs. existing singular `quickmark-*`/`bookmark-*` commands) and the fact that `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` directly, bypassing `QuickmarkManager.clear()`'s `removed` signal emission. Test coverage is thin for QuickmarkManager specifically, and the feature scenarios lack descriptive names. Documentation/changelog updates appear missing.
